entries.note: mew07, a friendly arched mew, 0.29 to 0.67 s (the mew proper; verified from the audio). Quiet at the source, so the build lifts it.
mew22, a soft mew with a purr-like rumble just before it, 0.10 to 0.60 s. The nearest Tabby has to a purr-meow: her real purrs sit below the 100 Hz high-pass.
exhale5, a short low half-growl, 0.12 to 0.38 s: her rar exhale, not a hiss.
squeak13, a steady flat squeak, with the 5 Hz wobble.
squeak03, the squeak she made when poked while resting, 0.41 to 0.80 s.
squeak17, a strong squeak that rises at the start: one of her best-recorded clips.
mew06, a mew that already glides down, with the falling pitch ramp (0 to -4 semitones). Faint at the source.
mew18, her clearest plain old-cat meow, flat then a slight lift, 0.07 to 0.48 s.
mew21, the clip the uploader labelled with a question mark, with a rising pitch ramp (0 to +3 semitones). Starts on the first sample; the build's 3 ms fade-in covers it.
squeak15, a chesty squeak with some body under it, 0.035 to 0.38 s.
squeak14, a tiny croaking squeak, clean, 0.11 to 0.41 s.
Borrowed from lolamadeus: one whole snore (7.65 to 8.64 s) with silence either side; Tabby has no snore of her own.
mew04, a steady rough-edged mew down two semitones: a questioning 'hm'.

Borrowed from jsbarrett: the loudest of the eight trills in the file, whole (9.84 to 10.21 s). A real trill, kept on purpose instead of the made-in-code 12 Hz chatter the other sets use, so there is a recorded alternative to hear.
mew09, an impatient grumbly mew with a low rar, then the tail thump.
